3.text: as I myself had occasion to witness. Possibly this may be due to the fact

4.text: that the Chukchee have a taboo against the use of fire-arms on the wolf, and

5.text: will use only a lasso or a trap for killing it.

6.text: THE HERDSMAN’S WORK. — On the open, stormy tundra the Chukchee

7.text: herdsman, who has no watch-dog, has a considerable amount of trouble with

8.text: his half-wild herd. The reindeer are only half domesticated, and ready to

9.text: disperse on the first occasion. When left to themselves in the open tundra,

10.text: they soon become quite wild, and even more wary than the wild reindeer,

11.text: since they know the ways of man. Every now and then, when going to a

12.text: fresh pasture or wandering over the tundra, some wayward animals will start

13.text: in the wrong direction, and the herdsman has to head them off. The herd,

14.text: therefore, progresses but slowly; and the more slowly, the larger the number

15.text: of animals. The highest praise for a herdsman is to say that his herd moves

16.text: along swiftly; like “the small cluster of a poor man,” to employ the usual

18.text: During certain seasons, especially with the coming of insects, the herd

19.text: requires the utmost exertion of everybody in the camp, including girls and

20.text: married women. The latter, though not very active, are able to relieve the

21.text: men for a little while, so as to give them their much-needed rest. The herd

22.text: will not stay on the same spot, even for a short time, but wants to move

23.text: against the wind to find relief from insects. When stopping for a while, only

24.text: the centre of the herd stands quietly. The outer animals move swiftly around

25.text: it — now from left to right, then from right to left — as if performing a

26.text: dance, and then suddenly dash forward against the breeze, carrying along the

27.text: whole herd. When the herdsmen are too few for regular watches, they may

28.text: not get time to sleep for two or three days in succession, and often are so

29.text: tired that they drop to the ground and fall asleep against their will. The

30.text: worst weather is a heavy warm fog without wind, because then the insects

31.text: are most troublesome, and the herdsmen cannot watch the movements of the

32.text: distant animals. At such times a herd may easily be lost, if the herdsman

33.text: should fall asleep even for a moment. To find its tracks in summer is no

34.text: easy matter; and the reindeer may either disperse, small bands joining neigh-

35.text: boring herds, or, in more lonely districts, run wild again. After the small-pox

36.text: epidemic of 1884 on the western Kolyma tundra, so many domesticated herds

37.text: ran free and dispersed, that their descendants may be recognized even now

38.text: among the wild reindeer at the mouth of the Kolyma. The wild reindeer in

39.text: Asia is uniformly gray. All those having black or white spots are descended

40.text: from the domesticated race. The best qualities of a herdsman are endurance

41.text: in walking, and ability to go without sleep for a long time.
